request.spec: Consolidate all duplicate detection into a single derived 'identityKey' = normalizedTelephone + '|' + (email or empty) + '|' + householdId, and reject with 409 only when a new owner's WHOLE identityKey equals an existing owner's. This changes existing behaviour: the separate telephone, email and household duplicate checks must now be expressed through this one key. Because the telephone is part of the key, two members of the same household (same householdId) with different telephones have different identityKeys and must both be allowed; only an exact full-key match is a duplicate. Return 'identityKey'.

agent.result_text:
Green. Both findings addressed; tests pass.

## What I changed

**Finding 1 — `keyOf` was speculative public API: agreed, fixed.**
There was no caller outside `of(Owner)` (the mapper and the check both use `of`). I folded the normalization logic directly into `OwnerIdentity.of(Owner)` and removed the separate `keyOf(String, String, String)` entry point entirely, so the class now advertises exactly one public method — the single "source of truth" its Javadoc describes.

**Finding 2 — mapper depending on a pipeline-function class: agreed, fixed (with a note).**
I moved `OwnerIdentity` into the `model` package, next to `MembershipLevel` — the existing precedent for a model-level `Owner` derivation that the mapper consumes (`MembershipLevel.of(owner)`). The mapper expression now reads `...model.OwnerIdentity.of(owner)`, so the mapper depends only downward on `model`.

One thing the review didn't anticipate: moving `OwnerIdentity` *alone* would not have fixed the inversion — it depends on `OwnerTelephone.toE164` for the spec-mandated "normalizedTelephone" component, and `OwnerTelephone` lived in `rest.function.owner`. Leaving it there would have just converted a `mapper → function` dependency into a `model → function` one, which is worse (model is the lowest layer). So I also moved `OwnerTelephone` — a pure, dependency-free normalization utility — into `model`. Now both the mapper and the pipeline check reach only into `model`, with no upward edges. This goes slightly beyond the reviewer's "`OwnerTelephone` can stay put" remark, but it's the only way to land `OwnerIdentity` in the model layer without introducing a new inversion.

While moving `OwnerTelephone` I also cleaned up its Javadoc, which still referenced the deleted `CheckOwnerTelephoneUnique` class, and updated the `{@link}` references in `ValidateOwner` and `AssignHousehold` to match the new package.

Acceptance behaviour is unchanged: `coreRejectsIdentityCollision` and the full suite pass (`BUILD SUCCESS`).

code_review.final_verdict:
VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED

The consolidation itself is well-executed and idiomatic: one `OwnerIdentity` helper, one `CheckOwnerIdentityUnique` step, one exception, one handler, one escalation YAML — mirroring the single-responsibility step pattern the codebase already uses, with the check correctly repositioned after `AssignHousehold` and clearly documented. Two structural issues keep it from clean, though:

**1. `OwnerIdentity.keyOf(String, String, String)` is public but has no caller (speculative API surface).**
The only production consumers are `CheckOwnerIdentityUnique` and `OwnerMapper`, and both call `of(Owner)`. `keyOf` is invoked only internally by `of`. Exposing a second public entry point with no external use adds API surface a maintainer has to reason about and keep in sync ("which one do I call, and why are there two?"). Unless something outside this diff (e.g. a test) genuinely needs the raw-component form, make `keyOf` private and let `of` be the single public "source of truth" the class's own Javadoc advertises. If a test does use it, that's worth a one-line note on the method so the public-ness is explained rather than looking accidental.

**2. `OwnerIdentity` lives in `rest.function.owner` but is now consumed across layers.**
With the mapper mapping added, `OwnerMapper` (mapper layer) now reaches into `rest.function.owner` — the request-handling layer — to compute a DTO field. The other mapper expressions reference model-level derivations (`MembershipLevel.of`, `Regions.localityOf`, `ContactPreference.of`). `identityKey` has become a genuinely cross-cutting derived attribute of an owner (used by both the responder/mapper and the pipeline check), so its home in the function package is now a slight layering inversion. Consider whether it belongs alongside those model-level derivation helpers instead, so the mapper doesn't depend on a pipeline-function class. This is lower-severity than (1) — the existing `OwnerTelephone`/`OwnerHousehold` helpers already sit in that package — but the new mapper dependency is what tips it over.

Neither is a correctness issue; fixing (1) at minimum would make the new class read as intended.
